evidenceAudit.scope: Adult acute pancreatitis in India: diagnosis, severity (Revised Atlanta), fluid resuscitation, nutrition, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) for cholangitis, antibiotics only for infected necrosis, cholecystectomy timing in gallstone pancreatitis and alcohol counselling, using the ACG guideline (2024), the NCDC-ICMR antimicrobial guideline (2025) and the ICMR Gall Stone Disease STW (2022).
findings: Diagnosis (two of three), computed tomography (CT) only when unclear or not improving at 48–72 hours, Revised Atlanta grades, organ failure markers, risk factors for severe disease, lactated Ringer's at up to 1.5 mL/kg/hour with 10 mL/kg boluses for hypovolaemia, early oral feeding, enteral over parenteral nutrition, no prophylactic antibiotics, ERCP within 24 hours for cholangitis and same-admission cholecystectomy checked against ACG 2024.
Infected necrosis regimens and no antibiotics for sterile pancreatitis checked against NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 section 4.9; cholecystectomy timing against the ICMR Gall Stone Disease STW (July 2022).
unverifiedSections: No ICMR STW dedicated to acute pancreatitis was found.
Analgesic choice and doses are not in the opened sources; use local analgesia protocols (opioids are acceptable).
Paediatric acute pancreatitis is outside the scope of the cited sources.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Acute pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas caused mainly by gallstones and alcohol in India; others include hypertriglyceridaemia, hypercalcaemia, drugs, trauma and post-ERCP. Premature activation of trypsin inside acinar cells digests the gland and triggers a systemic inflammatory response that can cause capillary leak, hypovolaemia and organ failure. Most attacks are mild and settle in days; severe disease with persistent organ failure (over 48 hours) carries high mortality (ACG 2024). Early care is fluid resuscitation with careful reassessment, pain control, early feeding, and treating the cause; antibiotics are only for infection (ACG 2024; NTG 2025).
keyMechanisms: Duct obstruction or alcohol triggers premature trypsinogen activation in acinar cells.
Autodigestion and cytokine release cause local necrosis and systemic inflammation.
Capillary leak causes hypovolaemia, haemoconcentration and organ failure.
Necrotic tissue can become infected, usually after the first week.

symptoms: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back
physicalSigns: Jaundice if a common bile duct stone
redFlags: Organ failure lasting over 48 hours: severe pancreatitis
Fever, jaundice and pain: cholangitis needs ERCP within 24 hours (ACG 2024)
precipitants: Alcohol (usually over 50 g/day for over 5 years) (ACG 2024)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Free gas under the diaphragm; board-like rigidity.
Right upper quadrant pain and Murphy's sign; lipase normal or mildly raised.
Pain out of proportion; lactate high; CT angiography.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Two of three: typical pain; lipase or amylase above 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN); characteristic imaging.
No organ failure and no local complications.
Transient organ failure resolving within 48 hours and/or local complications.
BUN 20 mg/dL or more, haematocrit 44% or more, BMI above 30, age over 55, altered mental status, SIRS.

clinicalManagement.title: Fluid resuscitation
actions: Lactated Ringer's in preference to normal saline (ACG 2024 recommendation 4).
Hypovolaemic: 10 mL/kg bolus; otherwise up to 1.5 mL/kg/hour (ACG 2024).
Reassess within 6 hours and over 24–48 hours: aim for falling BUN; watch for fluid overload (ACG 2024).

clinicalManagement.title: Pain and monitoring
actions: Adequate analgesia (opioids acceptable) per local protocol.
Monitor for organ failure in the first 48 hours; intensive care unit (ICU) for persistent organ failure.

clinicalManagement.title: Nutrition
actions: Mild: oral low-fat solid diet within 24–48 hours as tolerated (ACG 2024 recommendations 10–11).
Moderately severe or severe: enteral feeding (nasogastric acceptable); avoid parenteral unless enteral fails (ACG 2024).

clinicalManagement.title: Biliary cause
actions: No cholangitis: medical treatment rather than ERCP within 72 hours (ACG 2024 recommendation 5).
Mild or moderate gallstone pancreatitis: laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the same admission (ICMR GSD STW; ACG 2024).
Severe: cholecystectomy 4–6 weeks after resolution (ICMR GSD STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Antibiotics
actions: No prophylactic antibiotics, including severe or sterile necrotising pancreatitis (ACG 2024 recommendation 8; NTG 2025).
Suspect infected necrosis with deterioration after the first week: start antibiotics, take surgical opinion; delay drainage to about 4 weeks if stable (ACG 2024; NTG 2025).

clinicalManagement.title: Prevent recurrence
actions: Alcohol cessation counselling; treat hypertriglyceridaemia or hypercalcaemia.

branches.label: Infected pancreatic necrosis
branches.entryCriteria: Infected necrosis or infected pseudocyst (clinical deterioration, gas on CT, positive culture).

regimens.dose: 10 mL/kg bolus if hypovolaemic; otherwise up to 1.5 mL/kg/hour
regimens.duration: 24–48 hours, guided by BUN and clinical response
adjustments: Paediatric: Paediatric fluid rates not in the cited source.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Caution and frequent reassessment in kidney disease (ACG 2024).
CLD: Caution in cirrhosis with ascites.
contraindications: Fluid overload in cardiac or renal disease (ACG 2024)
Hypercalcaemia: avoid calcium-containing fluid until corrected

medicationPlan.note: Fluid strategy from ACG 2024; infected necrosis regimens and no-antibiotic rule for sterile pancreatitis from NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 section 4.9. Add antifungal cover only if risk factors for invasive candidiasis (NTG 2025). India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Diagnose with two of three criteria.
Use antibiotics and ERCP only when indicated.
keyPoints: Lipase above 3 times ULN plus typical pain is enough; CT is not routine.
Lactated Ringer's, up to 1.5 mL/kg/hour; reassess at 6 hours.
pitfalls: Sending mild gallstone pancreatitis home without cholecystectomy.
